messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the angular velocity of the pendulum and the damping coefficient of the surrounding fluid. Fluid resistance is characterized by the viscosity of the medium, the shape and size of the body, and the rate of its motion. Motion in a real environment always encounters some form of resistance that opposes the swing. Swing amplitude gradually diminishes when the damping torque is not negligible compared to the gravitational restoring torque. Torque from viscous friction must be included in the physical pendulum model when the oscillations are damped and the energy loss per cycle is significant. Significant damping occurs, for example, when the pendulum swings in a thick fluid or when the motion is very fast. Fast motion in air still produces measurable drag, so even for a simple pendulum in air the viscous term should be retained for accurate long-term predictions.
